description: A long one-line opening message (streamed fast, taller than a phone viewport), then sixteen one-command tool rounds that fold one by one as each completes, then new prose that streams slowly. The moment that prose starts, the opening line is no longer the latest word: it folds into the run with the commands, shrinking the transcript above a reader following the live edge by more than a phone viewport.

steps.text: Checking the project step by step, starting from the top level and working down through each part in turn, so that nothing is skipped and every result can be compared with the one before it. The first pass looks at the layout of the repository as a whole, which folders hold the application code, which hold the tests and which hold the scripts that build and package everything, and it notes anything that looks out of place for a project of this shape. The second pass reads the configuration files one at a time, the settings for the build, the settings for the test runner and the settings that decide which checks run on every change, and it compares each value with what the rest of the project expects to find there. The third pass runs a short command for each area, one command per area and one area per round, so that a failure points at exactly one place and the output of every round stays small enough to read at a glance. After that the commands repeat for the parts that depend on the earlier ones, the database layer, the request handlers, the background jobs and the pieces that talk to other services, again one short command at a time with nothing run in parallel. Every round reports what it found in a single line, the work keeps going until all sixteen commands have finished, and only then does a short summary follow that says what passed, what failed and what to look at next, written for someone who was not watching while the checks ran and wants the outcome first and the detail afterwards.

All sixteen checks ran. The new paragraph starts here and streams slowly, so a reader following the live edge should keep seeing it arrive at the bottom of the screen while the long opening line above it folds into one line with the commands. It keeps going for a while longer to leave time to look at the screen during the stream. Done.
